title: A joint acid-base chemistry hinge does not improve low-grip prediction in a second NHANES survey
abstract: We tested an exploratory joint low-bicarbonate/high albumin-corrected-anion-gap feature beyond individual chemistry markers and anthropometry in older adults. Frozen logistic models trained in NHANES2011-2012 (1315 participants;89 low-strength cases) were evaluated in separately recruited NHANES2013-2014 (1466;98 cases). Target weighted Brier score was 0.04174411 without versus 0.04174652 with the feature; delta +0.00000240, joint rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.00015440,+0.00080062]. Only39 training and27 target participants had positive feature values. No incremental predictive benefit was demonstrated. Sparse joint abnormalities, prior survey exposure and same-program validation limit precision and generalization; this is not equivalence or a test of treatment.
